title: Maryland Murder Suspect Hid With Help From His Mom After Deadly Kidnapping, Police Say - NewsBreak
text:
By Zak Failla ,
10 hours ago Justin Michael Green Collins Photo Credit: Montgomery County Department of Police/Google Maps Justin Michael Green Collins, 25, was located at a home in District Heights and arrested in Washington DC, where he was taken into custody in connection with the death of 29-year-old Akwalabeng Fontava inside his North Bethesda apartment in September 2025.
Officers from the Montgomery County Department of Police were called around 7:40 a.m. on Sept. 21, 2025 , to the 5900 block of Montrose Road for a reported medical emergency.
Inside, first responders found Akwalabeng Fontava with a fatal gunshot wound.
He was pronounced dead at the scene.
But the case didn’t stop there.
Detectives learned that a man and woman were allegedly kidnapped and forced into a vehicle after the shooting.
Police said the man was later released in Silver Spring.
Investigators tracked the car to Westfield Montgomery Mall, where they found the woman with Sheldon Milan Boykins, 37, of Hyattsville, who was arrested that same day.
The second suspect, Joshua Carter, was apprehended in Fayetteville, North Carolina, at a family member’s residence. He was extradited to Montgomery County on Oct. 24, 2025.
Collins’s mother, 46-year-old Shatym Neko Sanderson, of Silver Spring, was arrested on Nov. 12, 2025, and charged with accessory after the fact to first-degree murder.
Homicide detectives determined that Collins’s mother helped him financially while he was on the run.
Sanderson was released in January 2026 on a $5,000 unsecured personal bond.
Collins is being held in DC on handgun possession charges related to his arrest on Tuesday, March 17.
Both Boykins and Carter are currently being held without bond at the Montgomery County Central Processing Unit, where they are awaiting trial.
